cards.explanation: The answer is True. The Galileans welcome Him. That's the plot twist, friends. You hear that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown, and you brace for a cold shoulder, and then the Galileans welcome Him. John adds that they had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well. Hometown crowds can surprise you.
The answer is Jerusalem. The Galileans had gone to the feast, and they saw the great things Jesus did there. So when He showed up in Galilee, they weren't hearing it secondhand. They were there.

The answer is that He turned the water into wine. Cana, the water into wine town. John doesn't just say Jesus came to Cana. He says He came once again, to the place where He had turned the water into wine. That's a place with a history.

The answer is begs, friends. That's the word John uses. John 4:47 says the official went and begged Jesus to come down and heal his son. He's a royal official, and he's down to begging. That tells you how badly he needs help.

The answer is True, friends. John 4:47 says the official's son was about to die. It's the same verse where the official goes and begs Jesus to come down and heal him. I think a father hears that and just starts moving.

The answer is that he says to come down before his child dies. He says, "Sir, come down before my child dies." (John 4:49) Jesus just said something that could have stung, and the father keeps his eyes on his boy. I think that's a man who has one thing on his mind.

The answer is that he takes Jesus at His word and leaves. John says it plainly: the man took Jesus at His word and departed (John 4:50). Jesus hadn't agreed to come down, and the father went anyway. All he had were the words "Your son will live." and he headed home with them.
The answer is False, and thank goodness. John 4:51 says his servants met him on the way with the news that his boy was alive. That's the word he needed on that road.

The answer is that he asks what hour his son got better. John 4:52 says he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered. Good news landed, and he still wanted to know exactly when it happened. I think that's a man who is connecting dots.

The answer is that it's when Jesus said his son will live. The seventh hour matched. The father realized it was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, "Your son will live." (John 4:53) Same hour, no gap. And John says he and all his household believed.
The answer is household. John 4:53 says he and all his household believed. It wasn't only the dad who walked away changed. The whole home came along.

The answer is second. John 4:54 calls it the second sign Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee. The first was at Cana, when He turned the water into wine (John 2:11). Cana got both of them, and I'm a little jealous.
